summary: Static review found no blocking implementation defect in the scoped delivery/lifecycle design. One existing coalescing test still uses separate wall-clock samples and can fail under scheduler delay. New regression fixtures otherwise use deterministic barriers and completion acknowledgment. No tests were executed.

findings.claim: The persistent worker, bounded ring, and scalar loss state preserve admission order without callback-created tasks. In-flight event/byte reservations survive reset and release only in complete(). Pending loss blocks later admission until its ordered marker is dequeued, so overflow becomes visible even without another callback.
findings.recommendation: Retain these invariants. Treat byte accounting as the documented payload estimate, not an RSS guarantee; raw input and normalized output each have their own bounded owner.

findings.claim: Actor-serialized runtime calls and revocable epochs fence async start continuations, retained callbacks, and held deliveries. Startup callbacks remain staged until runtime.start succeeds; throwing startup discards them. Authentication precedes managed state/data mutation, and bridge receive has no suspension between its epoch check and mutation. No observer-retaining worker capture is visible.
findings.recommendation: Keep the distinction between synchronous epoch revocation and stop completion: receive already past its epoch check may finish before the bridge processes stop, while stop awaits that bridge transition. Existing held-delivery tests correctly exercise work that has not crossed this commit boundary.

findings.claim: DiskStewardEndpointTests.swift:43-44 constructs the intended 0.2-second coalescing gap from two separate Date() samples. If the test is descheduled for more than roughly 0.8 seconds between them, the gap exceeds the one-second window and the coalescing assertion fails. This residual nondeterminism predates the candidate but remains in its regression suite.
findings.recommendation: Use one fixed base Date for the first event and base.addingTimeInterval(0.2) for the second. No scheduler-dependent delay should determine this oracle.

findings.claim: The new fixtures explicitly cover held-first ordering with an excluded middle event, count/byte bounds including old in-flight ownership across restart, overflow without a later callback, retained callbacks, stop/crash, superseded activation, synchronous startup failure, filtered/invalid gaps, sequence/arithmetic overflow, auth, coalescing replacement bytes, and deinit cleanup. Assertions follow barriers and waitUntilIdle rather than sleeps. Static inspection supports the intended AC523 cases but does not establish runtime test success.
findings.recommendation: Join coordinator full-suite results and reconcile the timestamp fix before acceptance. Native callback concurrency/order and entitlement behavior remain platform-validation limitations, not defects demonstrated by these fixtures.
